60201801.text: Ah, Lord Sangemah Bay. How lovely to see you.

60201802.text: I must thank you for the device you provided, it was an enormous help. Would I be right in thinking that it was developed by the Akademiya?

60201803.text: Why come and ask me when you clearly know already?

60201804.text: I mostly came to thank you.

60201805.text: Hehehe, that's more like it. A little gratitude goes a long way with Lord Sangemah Bay... Play your cards right, and you might even stand a chance of becoming my long-term supplier.

60201806.text: The chance to work with such a kind and charitable investor as yourself would be a great honor for the Curatorium.

60201807.text: Huh? Charitable? Who said anything about charity? First I'm hearing about it.

60201808.text: Let's see... The first plot of land you purchased in Nod-Krai, your desert interests, and—

60201809.text: Pshh, tshhh, stop! What do you think you're doing, exposing my investment history!?

60201810.text: It's nothing to hide from. They're all perfectly legitimate investments. And some of the land you purchased was with the intent of building a sanctuary... Yes, I heard about that too.

60201812.text: You're a curious case, Lord Sangemah Bay. You don't like people finding out about your good deeds, do you?

60201813.text: But I'm afraid no matter how hard you try to keep things under wraps, where there's a will, there's a way.

60201815.text: You did it for Sumeru, didn't you?

60201816.text: It was empty land that was gonna go to waste otherwise. I figured if I built something there, it might at least get some use in an emergency.

60201817.text: Disasters are capricious things. They strike without any warning. I've lost family to a disaster before, and I don't want to lose any friends or business partners if I can help it.

60201818.text: My elder sister used to dream of finding a sanctuary. Somewhere with plenty of food, water, and medicine, where everyone could live happy lives.

60201819.text: It was something I looked into. But after discussing things with the Dendro Archon, I decided on a more effective strategy.

60201820.text: The tech people handled the tech, and moneybags provided the Mora. It just made the most sense.

60201821.text: It's a pity that so few people know the truth about you. Everyone says that you view everything in terms of Mora, and all you care about is growing your own wealth.

60201822.text: So? What's the problem with that? Everyone wants to be rich — it's human nature. So yes, I love Mora, and it's nothing to be ashamed of.

60201823.text: But surely you have dreams of your own beyond just making Mora?

60201824.text: You don't get it, do you? My dream is to invest in other people's dreams. And, y'know make a nice little slice for myself along the way.

60201825.text: Ah, just thinking about it makes me happy... that sweet, sweet sound of Mora...

60201829.text: Oh, that... I was just returning a favor. Don't worry about it.

60201830.text: Seems like we've both been away from home for a very long time.

60201831.text: Yeah... so long that I barely remember what my family even look like.

60201832.text: That would be your mother, father, and sister...?

60201833.text: Yeah, though it's been years since my sister passed away.

60201834.text: It's not like I want to forget them, obviously. But memory can be even more ruthless than the most calculating businessperson. Beyond a certain point, if something isn't helping you, it just gets rid of it.

60201835.text: My sister can't help me now. Slowly but surely, her face is fading from my mind's eye. It's become a vague impression.

60201836.text: Not everything will fade. When loved ones pass away, the beautiful memories are the ones that last the longest.

60201837.text: Yeah, that's true. If you ask me, that's the one silver lining in all of it.

60201838.text: Well that, plus... I'm sure that life is much better now than it was back then?

60201839.text: Oh, absolutely. I have tons of Mora, a big, beautiful house, business is booming, and I'm as happy as can be!

60201840.text: You've got a lot going for you, too. Boss of the Curatorium of Secrets? I'm sure there's plenty of Mora to be made in that line of work!

60201841.text: I appreciate the vote of confidence.

60200101.text: Timed that pretty well, didn't I?

60200103.text: It's okay. I'm just glad no one was hurt.

60200104.text: Paimon noticed you doing something too, Dainsleif. Were you helping get them out?

60200105.text: Of course. When I asked Nefer to conduct this investigation, I was not naive to the dangers involved.

60200106.text: I had a duty to ensure your safety.

60200107.text: Heh, good to know your sense of justice is still intact after all these years.

60200108.text: I take that to mean that you saw the truth. That comes as a great relief.

60200109.text: I certainly did. And, thanks to your help, I also managed to trap Rerir inside the chess set.

60200110.text: Whoa, really? How'd you manage that?

60200111.text: Well, to be honest, I sensed that something was wrong long before we made it to the temple.

60200112.text: By using this fragment to probe into Rerir's past... well, the monster formerly known as Rerir... it seems I alerted him. I was tracking him, then he caught on and started tracking me too. Can't say I'm surprised.

60200113.text: But how did he track you through your thoughts alone? That shouldn't be possible...

60200114.text: Rerir was a secret agent who reported directly to the Vinster King. He is an expert at finding a trail and hunting down his pursuers.

60200116.text: He infiltrated the chess set, read my thoughts, and built a new, virtual chess set inside of it. That's why we weren't able to leave at first.

60200117.text: Speaking of your chess set, it's quite a remarkable item. Would I be right in thinking you have some connection to King Deshret?

60200118.text: You overestimate me. I only have a connection with one of his underlings, the Ibis King.

60200119.text: You all saw how this came to be. A long time ago, the Iab massacred my tribe, the Shimti, in our home village. A few years later, I enrolled in the Akademiya, where some new information came to light.

60200120.text: The Unut and the Iab fought a bitter battle over the rights to a well, all for the sake of a non-existent fifty million Mora. The Iab ultimately won that confrontation, but their victory came at the cost of almost every warrior in the tribe.

60200121.text: The final blow to the Iab came at the victory feast, when an Unut assassin beheaded their chief right before my eyes. The remaining Iab fled and have been scattered to the winds ever since.

60200122.text: Having gotten my revenge, I returned to my hometown, where — to my surprise — the nearby temple was still standing. There it was, seemingly immune to the relentless hostility of the desert, while my tribal home lay in ruins.

60200123.text: As I stood there, gazing at the temple, I noticed a cat just outside. This cat, as it turned out, was home to the spirit of the Ibis King. He led me to a gate deep inside the temple, and there he made a deal with me.

60200124.text: This chess set is my gift from the Ibis King. The chessboard within is made to the same specifications as the one in the Mausoleum of King Deshret, and represents his power of piercing analysis.

60200125.text: With this chessboard and its container, I gained a certain ability to perceive hidden secrets. Now, you could conclude that the Ibis King simply wanted to give the people of this world the power to seek the truth, but I don't believe that's the full story.

60200126.text: Every god plays favorites. Their hearts are as fickle as any human's — full of secrets, perversions, egotistical tendencies... But precious few gods are willing to admit this.

60200128.text: It is the same with all powerful forces, including fate itself. Their gaze falls preferentially upon a select few. As you rightly point out, this is an act of favoritism.

60200129.text: If you're alluding to the Abyss... then yes, I agree.

60200130.text: Gather the others. It's time to share everything I've learned.

60200131.text: Before long, the group is gathered in the office. Those too busy to attend inform the others of their movements...

60200132.text: Thank you all for being here.

60200133.text: As promised, I did some further investigating into the Rächer of Solnari's background. I am pleased to report that the investigation has been most fruitful indeed.

60200134.text: The Rächer of Solnari, real name Rerir, was once a Khaenri'ahn subject who served the Vinster King. I will now share the important details of his story — please save any questions or comments for the end...

60200135.text: Nefer narrates Rerir's backstory to the group.

60200136.text: At the Vinster King's behest, he gathered intelligence and assassinated descendants of the Crimson Moon dynasty. Unwilling to take down his beloved, Tholindis, who was secretly of Crimson Moon heritage, he then got dragged into court politics...

60200137.text: Vedrfolnir's voice, which spoke to him of his fate, was like a reflection of the moon. Though he could disturb the waters to gain some temporary relief, he was powerless to erase it entirely.

60200138.text: In contrast, Rerir's own life was like a reflection of a broken moon. Once the stormy winds of fate blew across the water's surface, it was utterly destroyed.

60200139.text: Tholindis smuggled away a piece of the moon before disappearing through that mysterious portal. It was passed down through the ages, finally falling into the hands of The Knave.

60200140.text: But what lies on the other side of that portal? Is it really a whole other world?

60200141.text: Tholindis never had the chance to share what she found there. Neither did Rerir, who followed her in.

60200142.text: So that's why he's so obsessed with the moon...

60200143.text: A tragic tale, to be sure. But it does not excuse his many transgressions.

60200144.text: No matter how much Rerir suffered in the past, the fact remains that he is what we know today as the Wild Hunt, wreaking havoc upon innocent lives in Nod-Krai.

60200145.text: He becomes more dangerous with each passing day. If left unchecked, it is simply a matter of time before all of Teyvat suffers the consequences. This is a threat that the Knights of Favonius cannot ignore.

60200146.text: A question for Miss Columbina. Forgive me if this is presumptuous, but have you ever seen the spatial gateway that appeared in Rerir's memory?

60200147.text: Never. But I have heard stories of something called the "Moon Gate," and this seems to fit the description.

60200148.text: Miss Lauma, any thoughts on this?

60200149.text: In the lore of the Frostmoon Scions, the moon is believed to hold many secrets. Some sources speak of ancient knowledge, others of a gateway to the unknown.

60200150.text: The term "moon gate" is one I have heard before. But, as is the case with all of our legends, there are no records of any firsthand witnesses. We cannot know whether it truly exists.

60200151.text: Then back to Miss Columbina. As a Moon Goddess yourself, do you have some idea of where the moon gate leads to?

60200152.text: Not at this stage, sorry. I do hold the power of the Frost Moon, and my strength is recovering well. I can sense that the gate would open at my command, but...

60200153.text: But there's more to the power of the Frost Moon than that?

60200154.text: Yes. A moon goddess has the right to open the moon gate, since it is a path to the moon. But as Nefer mentioned, holding open a spatial gateway takes a huge amount of power...

60200155.text: ...And right now, I need to conserve my energy to fight the Rächer of Solnari. I'm afraid this is one mystery we may have to leave unsolved for now.

60200156.text: I agree, better to save your strength. But if you'll humor me for a moment, I have a bold conjecture of my own regarding the world beyond the gateway.

60200157.text: I highly suspect that neither Tholindis nor Rerir made it through unscathed. The evidence pointing to this is the fact that the Rächer of Solnari exists in the form of countless fragments.

60200158.text: With the Abyssal power he wields, no ordinary foe can touch him, let alone tear him to shreds. And yet, the Wild Hunt proliferates wherever his scattered fragments lie, drawing hordes of monsters to many different locations across the land.

60200159.text: So your theory is that Rerir was physically torn to shreds by some powerful force — hence why the Wild Hunt is a distributed phenomenon rather than a unified one?

60200160.text: Makes sense to me. Explains why the Wild Hunt is so pervasive, and why he's been trying to piece himself back together. He was whole to begin with, and he wants to be whole again.

60200161.text: Without the power of the Abyss on his side, he almost certainly would have perished the moment he was torn apart. But the Abyss, much like a curse, has kept him alive...

60200162.text: ...I could not agree more. The power of the Abyss is most surely a curse.

60200163.text: It is a compelling explanation, and one that accords with my present understanding of Abyss creatures. Whether the lifeform in question is primitive or advanced, if a curse has extended its lifespan unnaturally, it will continue to survive in spite of everything.

60200164.text: This raises some interesting questions... I will run some experiments and see if there is any validity to my suspicions.

60200165.text: That being said, regardless of whether my research bears fruit, I would like to thank Miss Nefer for conducting such a thorough investigation. Already, it has greatly enriched my understanding of the entity we face.

60200166.text: My pleasure, Mr Albedo. I, too, hope that the information I have shared today proves useful as we look to formulate the next stage of our plan.

60200167.text: Hey... What is it, Dainsleif? You look really upset...

60200169.text: It's just... when I think of the man I once knew as Rerir, I struggle to understand why things had to turn out like this.

60200170.text: The two of you used to be friends, didn't you? I don't know if these words will bring any comfort, but... my heart goes out to you.

60200172.text: We can never know all the hows and whys of the way things are. The moon and stars are full of untold secrets and lies, and the skies are host to many more mysteries than these alone. Yet, none of that can begin to compare with the complexity of human life.

60200173.text: Those are the first comforting words I've heard in a long time. Thank you both.

60200174.text: Well, I think this is a good place to end today's meeting. I'm sure Nefer needs some time to recover — she's been through an awful lot today.

60200175.text: That's very thoughtful of you, Lauma.

60200177.text: Sounds good to me. Take some time to rest and digest before we reconvene to nail down a plan.

60200901.text: Hey... is this a bad time? Hope I didn't kill the conversation...

60200903.text: Haha, no need. C'mon, let's talk outside.

60200904.text: Mmm, nice room... Oh, I—I'm not coming in, though.

60200905.text: Why not? It's just a hotel room...

60200906.text: If it's all the same, I'll just stay out here. I might not look the part, but I am technically a knight. Barging into people's private quarters isn't the kind of thing we do...

60200907.text: Anyway, Nefer went back to the Curatorium to get some rest. But before she left, she shared some things with me that I thought you should be aware of.

60200908.text: Firstly, although she managed to trap the Rächer of Solnari inside her chess set, there's no guarantee that the power of the Ibis King is any match for one of the Five Sinners. Their powers are beyond our comprehension.

60200909.text: It's only a matter of time before he finds a way to break out. We have to come up with a plan and take care of him before that happens.

60200910.text: Honestly, Paimon figured that might be the case... So, how long have we got?

60200911.text: Heh, well... I asked her that same question. She talked for a long time, but for the most part, seemed like she was trying to convince me how precious her chess set is... and what a long and storied history it has.

60200912.text: Felt like some kind of sales pitch. You know, the kind where you end up handing over Mora against your will? ...Anyway, after all that, she finally answered the question: Two days, at most.

60200913.text: Two days!? Holy moly... Can we even recruit enough help in that time?

60200914.text: That remains to be seen. Which brings me to the second issue: Dainsleif is obviously conflicted about this whole thing, but given how little time we have, there's no way we can pull this off without his help.

60200915.text: You have some history with him, right? Do you think maybe you could... talk to him for us?

60200916.text: I'll see what I can do.

60200918.text: Alright, onto item three. So, Albedo, Durin, and I put our heads together and came up with a plan. Can't promise it's gonna work yet, but at least it's a start.

60200919.text: We figured we'd bounce the idea off you first. We'll explore it further once everyone's recovered.

60200921.text: Oh, Paimon's dying to hear this!

60200922.text: Alright, so... Here's what we're thinking...

60200923.text: In a hushed voice, Varka lays out the current plan.

60200924.text: It's a shocking plan... but nothing can faze the greatest Traveler and trustiest travel guide in Teyvat. It doesn't take you long to get behind it.

60200925.text: We felt a little uneasy about roping you into this... I mean, firstly, you're not locals, and secondly, none of us are your boss. You're well within your rights to refuse, if you so choose.

60200926.text: Roping us in? Why would you even say that? We know the stakes here — it's all of us against the Rächer of Solnari, or none of us stand a chance.

60200927.text: I choose my words very intentionally, I'll have you know. I like to think there's an art to striking a down-to-earth tone even when the stakes are through the roof.

60200928.text: Sir Varka, I have a few thoughts about this plan.

60200930.text: I think we can be more flexible with how the roles are allocated. In my view, the most sensible lineup would be like this...

60200931.text: I see your point, yeah. But if that's how we're gonna approach this... You'd better make sure you're ready.

60200932.text: ...To be clear, I don't doubt your abilities — far from it. I just want to make sure... Are you really willing to take all this on?

60200933.text: I want to do everything within my power. The Rächer of Solnari is a truly fearsome opponent, and if I do my part, it'll greatly reduce the risk for everyone else involved.

60200934.text: Well, that tracks with what I've heard. Jean's mentioned in her letters that you're so diligent, it's almost... abnormal.

60200935.text: As in, most people weigh up the risks and rewards in situations like this. But you seem to just march towards danger without a moment's hesitation.

60200936.text: Of course, everyone appreciates a fearless pioneer. But all that aside, I'm the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, and you're our Honorary Knight. I want to make sure your courage doesn't come at the expense of your safety.

60200938.text: I should be the one thanking you — it means a lot to have you on board. I'll give some serious thought to your suggestions.

60200939.text: Varka gives a very knightly bow and says he'll see you at the hotel again later. He has arranged for everyone to meet and finalize the plan of action.

60200940.text: In an effort to lighten the mood, he booked out the hotel for this meeting — so you could all chat over a drink.

60201001.text: ...This is a thorough plan, but I do have one last question before we take action: How can we be sure that our enemy won't leave the designated area?

60201002.text: Great question. Albedo's been hard at work analyzing Rerir and the Wild Hunt's behavioral patterns. His conclusions are as follows.

60201003.text: Firstly, from the earliest known confrontation until now, Rerir has never displayed any ability to manipulate the dimension of space. So it's unlikely he has any power in that domain.

60201004.text: Secondly, he seems to have a particularly strong vendetta against our group. If we put him in a fight-or-flight situation, he'll choose to fight every time.

60201005.text: Thirdly, finally, and most importantly: He is consumed by hatred, both for the moon, and for his enemies.

60201006.text: Turns out, we tick both of those boxes. We have a reincarnated moon in our ranks, and a spy who accessed his private memories without permission. He'll be baying for blood, not looking to escape.

60201007.text: As someone who's had their fair share of interactions with the Wild Hunt, those all seem like valid observations to me.

60201008.text: Understood. Then I will defer to the verdict of the group.

60201009.text: Well everyone, that's the plan in full detail. Albedo and Durin are carrying out their part as we speak.

60201011.text: Okay! Any firepower you need, I got you covered. Let's light this baby up!

60201012.text: The Frostmoon Scions are behind you as well.

60201014.text: ...No objections? Alright, then it's settled. This is the plan we're going with. Next up, an old tradition of mine: Anyone who wants to back out, now's your chance.

60201015.text: Wait, we can still back out of this!?

60201016.text: Everyone says things they regret, right? I don't want anyone feeling trapped because their mouth said "yes" before their brain had time to think things through.

60201017.text: A very "people first" approach. I hear that's common practice in the Knights of Favonius.

60201018.text: Heh, who'd you hear it from? Diluc?

60201019.text: Shh. We don't use people's real names at work. This contact will be known only as "Owl," please and thank you.

60201020.text: This plan can only work if everyone does their part. Flins and I will absolutely support it.

60201021.text: We shall indeed. You'll be glad you accepted our help.

60201022.text: Also — you are the last person I expected to see here, Miss Dori.

60201023.text: Hehe, it's not often I get called Dori in a work context. My peers usually call me Lord Sangemah Bay.

60201024.text: Sooo... the longer your name, the higher your net worth? Is that the idea here?

60201025.text: Ahahaha, in that case, Mr Flins here must be worth a fortune! That's right, I know your full name. It's—

60201026.text: The walls are thin here. I'd appreciate you keeping that a secret.

60201027.text: Okay, okay, fine. Ugh, I'm actually only here as a favor for someone else. Do you have any idea how much it would cost to hire me otherwise!?

60201028.text: Whoa... Does this mean someone out there actually has the power to boss Dori around?

60201029.text: It most certainly does not! We have a longstanding and mutually beneficial business partnership. She's actually the mom of a friend of yours.

60201030.text: Said mom supplied me with a great little trinket, but now that lady's ruined everything. If I don't start building a little goodwill now, my whole business in Nod-Krai is gonna go down the drain!

60201031.text: Okay, so what exactly is so special about this pendant?

60201032.text: It's a lucky charm that a great mage made for me. We have a business relationship, and she was worried that something bad might happen to me. So, she wanted me to have something that can store power to protect myself with.

60201033.text: I FINALLY got it all fully charged up with kuuvahki, and then Nefer went and used it all up at once! Gah, never lost so big in my life!

60201034.text: You're right, it was all my fault. I didn't mean to drain all the kuuvahki in the pendant, but I'll make it up to you.

60201035.text: You will? Um, um, well, in that case... how about you give me your chess set and we call it even?

60201036.text: Hehe, I knew you'd say that. Well, it's yours if you want it. In fact, take it now and I'll even throw in a free Rächer of Solnari. Deal?

60201037.text: Ughhh... You're putting me in a difficult position here...

60201038.text: It's a very useful thing to have around... but I have a funny feeling it won't be around much longer. I guess we'll see in a couple of days.

60201039.text: Ugh, looks like bankruptcy for me...

60201040.text: Hey, don't be so pessimistic. See this through and you never know, you might find a new business opportunity on the other side.

60201041.text: With an action plan in place, everyone chats among themselves before going their separate ways to get started on their work.

60201042.text: You and Paimon decide to check in and see how each stage of the preparations are going.

60200301.text: Dori! How are things going, feeling ready?

60200302.text: Oh, I was born ready. We only have two days — you think Lord Sangemah Bay would let an opportunity like this slip by?

60200303.text: Don't forget, when something's in high demand, the people with the goods on hand get to charge the highest price of all! Even higher than the sellers taking advance orders.

60200305.text: That's so pretty! Did you make it?

60200306.text: I had no idea you were so skilled with your hands!

60200307.text: Hahaha, no, I have a supplier. We go way back, so he made me a very attractive offer.

60200308.text: Aha! No wonder you were talking about lucky charms at the meeting... You've been getting Kaveh to make them for ya!

60200309.text: Ehh, that's not the full story. It actually started a while back as a project between me and the Dendro Archon.

60200310.text: Mage Alice once warned me that this world won't stay safe forever. There may come a day when everyone faces a great crisis.

60200311.text: I passed this onto the Dendro Archon, and she secretly brought together a research team made up of Sumeru's top scholars to invent a technology that could keep people safe. I won't go into the details, because it's all very complicated — but if you wanna know more, you can ask the Dendro Archon about it some time.

60200312.text: Anyway, point being, it was the Dendro Archon who asked Kaveh to build this little contraption. As one of the top Kshahrewar talents, he was the obvious choice.

60200313.text: Took him long enough. He stressed over it for ages. Must have gone through at least a dozen designs before producing a final product... *sigh* But that's Kaveh for you.

60200314.text: Mehrak delivered it to me a couple of days ago, along with a letter from Kaveh... "Could I ask why I'm sending this technology to you? What's your proposed use case? Has it been approved by the relevant authorities?"

60200315.text: So nosy! Ugh, my fault for sending him the research permit to begin with!

60200316.text: Surely, Nahida must've told him you were involved in this project? He was probably just nervous 'cause you're always so secretive about your business.

60200317.text: Could be, could be. Anyway, I just replied: "Let's hope there never has to be a use case, because it would involve grave danger."

60200318.text: Fair enough. But it sounds like he was just being cautious. He probably felt responsible as the one who made it.

60200319.text: Or maybe he was asking as a favor for his housemate — he's done that before. Not sure why though. His housemate doesn't seem to really care that much about this kind of stuff.

60200320.text: Either way, all's well that ends well. I'm just glad to finally have my hands on the product. I wouldn't want to be without it given the potential dangers that lie ahead.

60200322.text: Uhh, Paimon's just... super surprised! This must be the first time we've ever seen you actually get serious about something...

60200323.text: This is not the Lord Sangemah Bay we're used to...

60200325.text: Well, a long time ago I made a promise to myself: I promised that I was gonna live every day of my life with a big beaming smile. Obviously, Mora plays a biiiig part in that... Ahem, buuut...

60200326.text: There are always gonna be times in life when you have to give something back. That could mean paying back a debt, returning a favor, or showing some kindness.

60200327.text: Alice has been a huge help to me over the years. She was the first investor I ever had, and I want my investors to know that Lord Sangemah Bay is the best in the business.

60200328.text: And more than that, no one knows what the future will bring. Whatever happens, I want to make sure the Dendro Archon and all of Sumeru is prepared to face whatever comes.

60200331.text: Oh, that? I was just making sure Nefer and I are square.

60200332.text: Don't be thinking it was some sort of benevolent act. I'm no saint, so don't treat me like something I'm not.

60200333.text: My priority is doing the business that I wanna do. So long as my conscience lets me, but... it usually does. That's the Lord Sangemah Bay business model.

60200335.text: I do say so, and that's the whole point. I'm a businesswoman. Don't go trying to figure out what kind of person I am, you'll exhaust yourself! Muuuch easier for everyone involved if you just take my word for it~

60200336.text: Oh, and could you two help me get this stuff where it needs to be? Thanks so much! You're my favorite assistants.

60200203.text: ...Sort of. As you're probably aware, Varka, Durin, and I captured some Abyssal creatures from the Wild Hunt.

60200204.text: Per the plan, we dissected and analyzed some samples of these creatures. The process went very smoothly... The findings, however, come with some troubling implications.

60200205.text: What!? You can actually dissect the Wild Hunt?

60200206.text: That depends on your definition of "Wild Hunt" and "dissection."

60200207.text: Harmless... lifeless... These words are accurate descriptions.

60200208.text: The Wild Hunt is an interesting phenomenon. In and of itself, it doesn't seem to possess anything akin to a human personality. But taken as a collective, the medium through which the Wild Hunt is summoned does appear to have a soul.

60200209.text: Master griped a lot about "The Wise" Hroptatyr, and seemed somewhat fascinated with "The Foul" Surtalogi. But she barely mentioned Rerir at all.

60200210.text: I don't think that was because of his lower social standing, though. Anyway, it's a pity — I should like to hear her thoughts on the nature of the lifeform he has become today.

60200211.text: It's a strange mix... the furious energy of an Abyssal being channeled through a fractured physical existence, a consequence of being torn apart by an unknown power...

60200212.text: Perhaps the only explanation for his survival in this state is that he sacrificed a degree of individuality in exchange for a continued existence...

60200214.text: Oh, sorry. Once I get talking about interesting research, I have a tendency to go on indefinitely.

60200215.text: Back to our research findings. Essentially, they confirm my hypothesis: Rerir's corpse is completely contaminated by the Abyss, and the effects are irreversible.

60200216.text: You could think of this as Rerir in mutated form — but in my view, even that would be inaccurate. In reality, his whole being has been consumed by the Abyss. In other words, he is now nothing more than a manifestation of Abyssal power.

60200217.text: Unfortunately, at present, we have no means of completely eradicating Abyssal power. Hence, we cannot fundamentally destroy the Rächer of Solnari either.

60200218.text: That's terrible news... So that's it, we can't defeat him? Not even if we get the power of the three moons?

60200219.text: Miss Columbina's situation is a difficult one. She can never achieve wholeness when the world does not accept her presence.

60200220.text: It's as if her creator banished her to a place she can never be accepted... It means, she spends most of her energy just on her own survival.

60200221.text: Given the circumstances, it's only natural to despair. But we must see this plan through to the end.

60200222.text: Time to kick off the backup plan.

60200223.text: Oh, Paimon almost forgot — this is for you. Dori asked us to bring it.

60200224.text: Ah, how wonderful. Well, thank you for making the trip. Durin and I will be heading off shortly.

60200225.text: I'm sorry I won't be there to protect you in person this time... Please be careful.

60201102.text: Yes. The fate of my flock is in your hands, Grand Master Varka. Please keep them safe.

60201103.text: My Lady... What are you saying?

60201104.text: Within the next twenty-four hours, we will face the biggest crisis the world has ever seen.

60201105.text: This is not a burden that we deserve to bear. But I believe that we reap what we sow in this life... So, I intend to act. I must do what I think is right.

60201106.text: For me, that means fighting for the future of Nod-Krai.

60201107.text: This gentleman is the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, Varka, Knight of Boreas. In my absence, please follow his lead.

60201109.text: Guess I should introduce myself. Hmm... Well, to start with, I know my way around a battlefield, hahahaha.

60201110.text: Biggest strengths are... honesty and hardworking-ness? Anyway, point is, I don't intend to let Lauma down. I'm gonna do everything in my power to keep every last one of you safe and sound.

60201203.text: Miss... Columbina, was it? I believe that's how the others addressed you.

60201204.text: That's right. Names are funny things... Have you always been called Dainsleif?

60201205.text: Yes... I take it your own name has a more complicated history?

60201206.text: I have a different relationship with names than other people. To be honest, I'm not even sure that "Columbina" is my name... at least, not in the same way that "Dainsleif" is yours.

60201207.text: But it's what everyone calls me, and I go along with it. A lot of my life has been that way... I get so used to things that I forget to question why they are so.

60201208.text: I never used to think much about where names come from, or what they mean to people... Maybe something's wrong with me.

60201209.text: You're different from other people. I sensed it the first time we met.

60201210.text: You're more perceptive than most. I'm sure your long life and rich range of experience explains that.

60201211.text: Do you ever find yourself missing Khaenri'ah, Mr. Dainsleif?

60201213.text: Difficult to answer. I have dreamed of the past many, many times. Sometimes I'm fighting tooth and nail, other times I'm lying on the ground, defeated.

60201214.text: I don't recall any happy moments from that time. It has been too long.

60201215.text: Is that because hatred survives longer than love and affection?

60201216.text: That would not be for me to say. I make no excuses for the grudges I bear. But whatever the reason, I remember little that was beautiful or sentimental.

60201217.text: ...Thank you for your help with the Rerir situation. Without your efforts, I never could have learned the hidden truth of his story.

60201218.text: You're welcome. I know he's your friend.

60201220.text: He betrayed me... and I never really understood what he was going through in life... Some friendship that is.

60201221.text: Okay. So, do you plan to fight him with us?

60201223.text: You see? You're torn. Now you know what really happened, you see the things he's done in a new light.

60201225.text: Of course — I completely understand. Anyone else in your position would feel conflicted too.

60201226.text: Actually, I went through something similar myself recently. Something happened that changed my perspective on a situation. A situation I took for granted at the time, but now I feel very grateful for it.

60201227.text: You mean the Harbingers who still support you, even though you've left the Fatui.

60201229.text: I always thought they were only helping me because Harbingers are forced to work together. But then I abandoned them. A warrant was even put out for my arrest...

60201230.text: Yet even now, they support me. Which means, I was wrong about them all along.

60201231.text: Clearly, they view you as a friend.

60201232.text: I feel a little guilty now. I regret not seeing their help for what it was... and not treasuring it.

60201233.text: I see the guilt that you're feeling now, because I feel it too. Hopefully, talking about it will do us both some good.

60201234.text: #...Have you noticed that {NICKNAME} and Paimon are over there? I think they've been listening.

60201239.text: Sorry... We were just concerned about you...

60201240.text: I apologize for making you worry.

60201241.text: No doubt you wish to know where I stand on the plan to take down Rer... the Rächer of Solnari. I'm afraid I need a little time. But I will seriously consider joining you.

60201242.text: You will? Thank you so much! Everyone will be so grateful to hear that.

60201243.text: They needn't be. This was something that I was going to have to face up to eventually.

60201244.text: That doesn't matter to them. They're grateful to you regardless.

60201245.text: You can't control their gratitude, so just accept it. And then, have a think about whether you're willing to join us.

60200401.text: Ah. You're earlier than I expected.

60200402.text: Hey, Flins. Been waiting here long?

60200403.text: Not too long. I came a little early so I'd have some time to think.

60200404.text: Are you nervous about the battle?

60200405.text: Quite the opposite... I'm reminiscing on my past battles.

60200406.text: When I was awakened by the Ratniki, I had not touched a weapon in many years. I felt like the battlefield was not where I belonged.

60200407.text: But after waging war against the Wild Hunt for so long, I came to realize something... A life of absolute peace is simply not a possibility for me.

60200408.text: My restless flame indicates that somewhere inside of me, there is a deep yearning to root out the evil in this world.

60200409.text: That doesn't sound like such a bad thing...

60200411.text: Well, in the past, when I was a fae whose primary concern was hibernation, it was hardly ideal.

60200412.text: But it certainly serves me well here in the present. And I am delighted to be able to join forces with you in this endeavor.

60200413.text: Looks like I'm not the first to arrive.

60200415.text: Did you sleep okay last night?

60200416.text: I struggled to settle down at first because of the nerves... But don't worry — I got enough sleep in the end. I'll be just fine.

60200418.text: Please. I'm just doing my part.

60200422.text: Aino asked me to relay a message. She said, Ineffa will be on high alert and keep a close watch over all secondary districts where defense is required, providing support as necessary.

60200423.text: Meanwhile, Aino herself will provide ranged support to us directly, using her latest invention.

60200424.text: Excellent. My thanks to all involved.

60200425.text: Uhh... The chess set's looking a little unstable...

60200426.text: It won't hold him much longer. We should be prepared to engage at a moment's notice.

60200427.text: No sense sitting around waiting. Let's make the first move while we still have the option.

60200428.text: I agree. Paimon, find a safe hiding place.

60200431.text: Everyone, take your positions as soon as the battle starts.

60200432.text: Every ounce of strength we have in our bones, let us bring to this fight.

60200438.text: Hah, I've seen all your futile ploys before. You have become the authors of your own demise.

60200439.text: I wouldn't be so sure about that.

60200440.text: You are merely a moment of sport before I tear down the moon.

60202002.text: Yes. I've thought a lot about it, and I've realized that you, me, and Arlecchino should be friends.

60202003.text: I think this is very important, so I felt I had to come and tell you.

60202004.text: Well, this is a new one. I'm so moved, I can't even hold my teacup... If that's all, you can leave now.

60202005.text: Do you not want to be friends with me? Or is it that you prefer being coworkers?

60202006.text: What is this, Columbina? Are you deliberately testing my patience threshold? Right now, my politeness module is active, but if you say another word, I swear I'll shut it down!

60202007.text: ...If your politeness module was active, wouldn't you say the word "please" at some point?

60202008.text: Pulonia, please see Lady Columbina to the door.

60202009.text: Will you still invite me to your next tea party?

60202011.text: ...Yes, I think you will. Bye-bye, dear Sandrone.

60202014.text: Last time, the Wild Hunt escorted you out. Would you rather I handled it myself this time?

60202015.text: We just wanted to... y'know, see how you were doing now that it's all over...

60202016.text: Why? Out of concern for my safety? Hah. I hope you didn't seriously think that the Rächer of Solnari would be able to lay so much as a finger upon me, given how prepared I was.

60202017.text: Mostly 'cause you kinda helped us out, so we just wanted to check you were okay. Looks like all your robots are fixed, huh?

60201901.text: How've you been holding up? Any adverse reactions? If you start to take a turn for the worse, make sure you tell me right away.

60201902.text: You don't need to worry about me, Grand Master. I'm fine. I mean, I barely did anything, so...

60201903.text: What? Hahaha, you're too humble, young man.

60201904.text: You played an indispensable role in the battle for Nod-Krai. We can't thank you enough for your support.

60201905.text: Sometimes, when people praise you, it's because you deserve it. The best thing is to accept it calmly and with grace. It's important to learn how to respond to words of admiration.

60201906.text: Let's do a quick demonstration: "Albedo, that was an incredible feat of alchemy! The pressure was on, but you worked flawlessly at lightning speed to get the job done!"

60201907.text: Thank you. I can't take all the credit, though — Durin played a big part in forming the alchemical array.

60201908.text: See? Did you catch that? A masterclass in how to take a compliment.

60201909.text: Umm... Okay, yeah, I did work pretty hard to help prepare for the battle. No point denying that.

60201911.text: Seriously, great work everyone. You all outdid yourselves.

60201912.text: #Hey, look who's bounced back! Looking good, {NICKNAME}!

60201913.text: Seems like you've recovered. You won't need to take any more medication.

60201914.text: Can I get you a drink?

60201915.text: Huh? You know how to order at a bar now? You've sure learned a lot recently!

60201916.text: Handling a drinks order is ridiculously simple compared to alchemy. Don't worry, I'll blend into society yet.

60201917.text: Paimon believes it! You're clearly a fast learner, just like your brother.

60201918.text: To be totally honest though, Paimon didn't quite follow all the details when you first explained the plan to us... Hehe...

60201919.text: Don't worry, that's completely understandable. Unless you're a student of alchemy, it's hard to grasp the principle and how the process works.

60201920.text: To put it in the simplest terms, we saw how our enemy stole the power of kuuvahki, and that gave us the idea of stealing his power to turn it against him.

60201921.text: When facing an enemy you have no hope of defeating, it's best not to engage them in battle.

60201922.text: So, instead of looking for a way to overpower him, we decided to help Columbina get strong enough to at least stand up to him in a fight.

60201923.text: For this to work, we had to analyze his modes of attack, confirm who his main target was, and make sure that he wouldn't go beyond the range of the alchemical array.

60201924.text: For added security, we prepared a total of four arrays, but to mitigate the impact of the battle, we identified one location in particular as the ideal spot, which is where the confrontation took place.

60201925.text: The alchemical array absorbed his Abyssal power, then Durin processed it to render it usable by Columbina.

60201926.text: That power enabled her to do what would otherwise have been nigh on impossible.

60201927.text: What surprised me was that Dainsleif actually agreed to join us.

60201928.text: Given his history with Rerir, he had every right to sit this one out... But we're extremely grateful for the decision he made.

60201931.text: It must have been a painful choice to make. But I'm sure that making a decision was far better for him than staying in limbo.

60201933.text: He was torn between two paths, but in the end, he made his choice and stuck to it resolutely. He doesn't strike me as the sort of person who'd stay trapped in limbo for long.

60201934.text: Anyway, however you cut it, everyone gave a stellar performance! And now it's time to kick back and celebrate!

60200503.text: They're fine. Apart from the blindness, of course.

60200507.text: Miss Nefer... It's not like you to lose your composure. That was the most reckless thing I've ever seen you do.

60200508.text: Reckless how? The situation was critical. Our lives were at stake. We had to do something.

60200510.text: *sigh* Okay, I guess you're right. Under the circumstances, it was a wise decision. You traded your eyes for an incredible victory.

60200511.text: In business terms, I suppose that's a huge return on investment.

60200512.text: I'd be hard-pressed to argue otherwise.

60200513.text: Still, I don't like this outcome. And I don't want you to lose your sight for good.

60200514.text: People suffer when they make sacrifices they shouldn't have to make. Whether that means faith, strength... or in this case, your ability to even see.

60200515.text: I had hoped you could win without sacrificing so much as a single hair on your head.

60200519.text: Don't try and open your eyes just yet. We'll see how you're doing in a couple of days. Until then, please follow your recovery plan to the letter.

60200520.text: I'll send full details through Jahoda. For now, just get yourself home, relax, and rest.

60200521.text: My dear friends, we have fought bravely and achieved a spectacular victory. A dark cloud has been lifted from the skies of Nod-Krai... All in this land will be grateful for what you have done.

60200522.text: The moon will remember this day. Thank you both.

60200523.text: Jahoda shows up and helps Nefer get home. And you, of course, have Paimon to escort you back.

60200524.text: The sight of Nefer navigating the road with her eyes closed is a new one for you. She proceeds cautiously, but as her silhouette disappears into the distance, you notice she seems almost smug.

60200525.text: There's something I want to let you know.

60200527.text: When Durin connected everyone's minds so I could access their powers, I also felt everything they felt.

60200528.text: And since Nefer's eyes were injured, my eyes are hurting now, too...

60200529.text: Huh? Hold on, let me try—

60200530.text: I only feel the pain, there's no actual damage. I just thought I should tell you.

60200531.text: ...Huh. You're right, there's no damage. That's a relief.

60200532.text: But I must say, I'm surprised to hear the Kuutar share something like this with me. In the past, you never used to open up about yourself.

60200533.text: Things are a little different now from how they were. I'm learning to share how I truly feel with my friends.

60200534.text: Friends... You have no idea how glad I am to hear that.

60200535.text: You can't help but break into a smile at the word "friends," as a warm and fuzzy feeling fills your chest.

60200536.text: One by one, your fellow teammates report in to inform you that everything is under control. At Lauma's insistence, you lie down. You fought on the front line against Rerir, and now you need rest.

60201302.text: Hah. Soon, you will be powerless to resist.

60201303.text: And then, I will reduce you to dust.

60201304.text: But that dust will plague your memories.

60201306.text: Any other tricks up your sleeve? Let's see them.

60201307.text: As entertaining as they are... You've backed yourself into a corner.

60201308.text: You don't fool me. I see your fear, clear as day.

60201309.text: (I have to stoke his rage! Make him unleash everything!)

60201310.text: You fear what you could never defeat. You fear the thought of never being able to save your beloved.

60201311.text: You cannot win the fight against fate, Rerir.

60201312.text: Hmph. Is that what you think?

60201313.text: Well, now it's your turn to feel afraid.

60201314.text: The only way to defeat Rerir is to borrow his own power.

60201315.text: That means Columbina will have to disappear while you two bear the brunt of his attacks.

60201316.text: You have to hold on. Find a way to keep him focused on killing the two of you.

60200602.text: How you feeling? Any aches and pains? Did you sleep well?

60200603.text: I'm doing alright, Paimon. No need to worry about me.

60200604.text: Phew, well that's good... Paimon's been sitting on the edge of the bed worrying about you for ages! You slept a whole day and night... Poor Paimon had to eat all by her lonesome...

60200605.text: Glad to hear you didn't starve. How was the food?

60200606.text: Well, it wasn't the same without you there to share it...

60200607.text: *sigh* Honestly, Paimon just can't relax when you're not your usual self. She couldn't enjoy the food and settle down to sleep.

60200608.text: Well, I'm back to normal now.

60200609.text: Oh yeah, and Albedo swung by earlier. He said to tell you to head to the tavern when you woke up. Varka and the others are organizing a victory feast, and they wanna celebrate with you.

60200610.text: He also dropped off some medical supplies, but you seem fit as a fiddle, so... hehe, guess you won't be needing those.

60200611.text: If you're feeling up to it, let's head over now! Wouldn't wanna keep them waiting!

60200703.text: Perfect timing! We were literally just saying how there's no way we're holding this victory feast without you. Any longer, and we would've postponed it till tomorrow!

60200705.text: Much better, thanks. Don't worry about me.

60200706.text: Relieved to hear it. If that changes, just let me know. Happy to check you over at any time.

60200707.text: Yep. We're here for you. Anything you need, just let us know.

60200711.text: I'm sure she'd love to catch up with you.

60200803.text: Much better, thanks to a good rest. You're looking well too.

60200804.text: Turns out that Moonchanter has some real talent, after all. My eyes were mostly recovered after just a couple days' rest. I can actually open them again now.

60200805.text: Yeah, but you gotta be careful... Lauma says not to strain your eyes while they're still healing.

60200806.text: Yes, thank you, I'm well aware.

60200807.text: Jahoda, could I borrow you for a moment? I could do with an extra pair of hands.

60200809.text: Did you hear that? I gotta go help Lauma for a second — you guys chat among yourselves. I'll grab us some drinks on the way back. Paimon, you still like 'em sweet?

60200810.text: You bet! Hehe, make it extra sweet, 'cause Paimon's earned it!

60200814.text: ...The Rächer of Solnari. Kind of a snake, don't you think?

60200815.text: Hmm... More of a wolf in my mind.

60200816.text: No, definitely a snake. A poisonous one, who spewed his venomous hatred everywhere.

60200817.text: Anyone who seeks revenge out of hatred for other people has become a snake. That's something my dad used to say.

60200818.text: I guess he didn't like seeing people go down the path of vengeance.

60200819.text: Perhaps. I'm sure it sounds like a very wise and open-hearted perspective to your ears. But me? I think hatred is a perfectly justifiable emotion.

60200820.text: What else is left when everything you depended on in life gets stripped away? Something's gotta fuel that drive to keep on living.

60200823.text: If you're worried about me, you can nip that in the bud. I'm not someone who gets stuck in the past.

60200824.text: It's just... I suddenly feel like I was wrong to call my father a liar. He was just a fool. That's why the Akademiya turned their back on him, and why the other tribes ganged up on him.

60200825.text: Oh, father... How much better things could have been if you were a skilled liar....

60200826.text: Look at the Ibis King... Thoth is a fiendishly cunning liar. And yet, strangely, he feels more like a father to me than my real dad ever was.

60200827.text: He's never brought it up, but I'd bet he feels the same way.

60200828.text: Why else would he give me the power to perceive the truth, while at the same time training me in the art of deception?

60201701.text: So, that "close colleague" who stayed behind with you... What's he been up to recently?

60201702.text: Don't know, don't care. I get more normal human interaction from hanging out with B.O.S.C.O. 2 than him.

60201703.text: Although, now you mention it, he hasn't bothered me in a while. I wonder if...

60201704.text: If he's disappeared without a trace, it's the biggest gift he ever gave to the world. But I somehow doubt that's what's going on.

60201705.text: He won't lie low forever... so we'd better stay on guard.

subQuests.subQuestName: Listen to what everyone is talking about
Listen to what everyone is talking about

60201402.text: #You bet! Snoozed {M#his}{F#her} way to a full recovery...

60201403.text: I'm doing much better. Thanks for checking on me.

60201405.text: A healthy body is paramount — nothing else in life is possible without it. So take it slow. You can't afford an injury.

60201406.text: I'm so grateful that you decided to help us in the end.

60201407.text: Paimon too! You really saved the day when you swooped in to open that gateway!

60201408.text: I came to accept that although Rerir was my friend in the past, here and now, he was an enemy that must be defeated.

60201409.text: Though I will never fully understand what happened between us, I could not let this crisis deepen any further.

60201410.text: We fought a very necessary battle. And you played your part admirably.

60201411.text: Thank you. I know it was hard, but you'll get through this.

60201412.text: Yeah! And if you ever need to talk, just remember, we're always here!

60201501.text: Hello you. Recovered from the battle?

60201502.text: Mostly recovered, thanks. I'm touched that you'd ask.

60201503.text: Come on, what do you mean? Of course I'm gonna ask! I care about my friends' wellbeing. And we are friends, aren't we?

60201504.text: Get yourself a drink, you've more than earned it! In fact, today, your drinks are on me. Lord Sangemah Bay's got you covered!

60201505.text: Wow, really? What about Paimon, has she earned it, too? Has she, pleeease?

60201506.text: #Hmm... Well, you haven't been through quite as much as {NICKNAME}, but... Ah, what the heck! Sure!

60201507.text: Yay! Wow, drinks on Dori — what a historic day!

60201508.text: Hey! Keep your voice down, or everyone else is gonna want in, too!

60201509.text: You, you... Have you heard anything I've been saying recently!? Doing business in Nod-Krai has been an absolute nightmare! If I'm buying for everyone, I'll—

60201510.text: Okay, okay, Paimon will speak more quietly. Geez...

60201512.text: Don't you forget, Lord Sangemah Bay doesn't just go around buying drinks for anyone and everyone...

60201601.text: I thought of a thousand ways to congratulate you, but... now you're here, words are failing me.

60201602.text: Hehehe, the Honorary Knight stuns them speechless once again!

60201603.text: Hahaha, well said. The Honorary Knight showed us all how it's done.

60201604.text: The other knights tell me that Mondstadt was the first stop on your journey. All of us are truly delighted to count you as our friend.

60201605.text: I'd like to thank you for supporting the Knights of Favonius, and also for helping us save Nod-Krai.

60201607.text: Nonsense! Of course I'm gonna mention it! This is more than just business — it's a relationship. And there can be no relationship without showing gratitude where it's due.

60209801.text: Back at the hotel, you sit with Paimon for a while and discuss what lies ahead.

60209901.text: It's nearly showtime... Let's go rendezvous with the others. You know the place!
